_: Methods the generator must NOT emit, and why (#78 step 6).
Read by gen_thunks.py, and every entry lands in gen/REPORT.md with its reason.
This is a declarative list the generator reads, deliberately NOT a patch applied
to generated output — a patch would be overwritten on the next run, and the
hand-written      a thunk in shim_pe.c already serves it. check_overrides.py
keeps this half of the list honest in BOTH directions:
every hand-wired method must appear here, and every entry
here must still be hand-wired. Delete a hand-written thunk
and the build tells you to drop its entry, whereupon the
semantic override the signature is generatable and forwarding it would still
be wrong. IsOverlayEnabled is the standing example: correct
code, wrong behaviour. These are the cases no signature can
express, so they have to be said out loud.

Hand-written in shim_pe.c and answered by a unix stub that unconditionally returns 1, which is what Proton does with the same wall (unixlib.cpp:231-239) (#90).

_marshal: Per-method marshalling facts the SIGNATURE cannot carry (ADR 0009).
A parameter pointing at a struct whose Windows and unix layouts genuinely differ
on x86_64 needs converting on the unix side. The conversion itself is mechanical --
Proton states both layouts field for field -- but two things are not derivable and
must be declared here or the generator refuses the method:
dir    in | out | inout. NOT derivable from const-ness: ISteamParties::CreateBeacon
takes a NON-const pointer that is an INPUT (the location to create a beacon
at), while the other five non-const cases are outputs. Converting an `out`
inward would read uninitialised PE memory; skipping the outward conversion
on an `in` would be harmless but skipping it on an `out` returns garbage.
count  how many elements the pointer addresses. Usually 1; where it is an ARRAY the
extent lives in another parameter, named by count_arg.
`arg` is the zero-based index among the arguments after `this`, and `param` is the
name it must have -- checked at generation time, so a version that renames or
reorders its parameters fails the build instead of marshalling the wrong one.

fills a caller-supplied ARRAY; the extent is the second parameter, not the signature
one location, written back to the caller
passed BY VALUE — the seam carries the address of the caller's copy, which is read and never written
one entry, written back to the caller
one details record, written back to the caller
